case_name: Krishan Chander Nayar v Chairman, Central Tractororganisation and Others
facts: The petitioner is a trained machineman who was employed as a machineman in the Central Tractor Organisation from 1948 until his services were terminated by notice dated September 16, 1954.
The petitioner appealed against the order of termination but his appeal was rejected on December 6, 1954.

After receiving a certificate stating that his services were terminated under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1949, the petitioner made several applications for appointment under the Government but without any results.
The alleged ban is contained in a memorandum dated September 21, 1955, which states that the Government regret their inability to lift the ban on his employment for the present.

The petitioner moved the Circuit Bench of Delhi of the High Court of Judicature for the State of Punjab under Art. 226 of the Constitution but his petition was dismissed in limine by the Division Bench of that Court by its order dated September 12, 1956, and an application for grant of the necessary certificate for appealing to this Court was also dismissed by the Bench on April 26, 1957.
This Court was moved under Art. 32 of the Constitution by a petition dated August 20, 1957.
issues: Whether the respondents had placed a ban on the petitioner being taken into Government service
Whether the petitioner's services were terminated in accordance with Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1949
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner was employed as a machineman in the Central Tractor Organisation from 1948 until his services were terminated by notice dated September 16, 1954.
The petitioner appealed against the order of termination but his appeal was rejected on December 6, 1954.

After receiving a certificate stating that his services were terminated under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules, 1949, the petitioner made several applications for appointment under the Government but without any results.
The alleged ban is contained in a memorandum dated September 21, 1955, which states that the Government regret their inability to lift the ban on his employment for the present.
respondent_arguments: The Central Tractor Organisation is a temporary organisation under the Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India

The petitioner was appointed as a purely temporary hand and his services were liable to termination at any time by giving him one month's notice or one month's pay in lieu of the notice and without assigning any reasons.
The ban alleged by the petitioner is purely a Departmental instruction for future guidance which did not prevent the petitioner from applying for any post under the Government.
court_reasoning: The affidavit on behalf of the respondents was unnecessarily verbose, misleading, and disingenuous

The respondents' answer to the petition does not make any reference to Annexure 'D' and ignores it, purporting not to admit that the respondents had put a ban on the petitioner being taken into Government service.

A person who has once been employed under the Government and whose services have been terminated by reason of his antecedents may not stand on an equal footing with other candidates not under such a ban.
holding: The Court holds that the respondents did place a ban on the petitioner being taken into Government service
The Court further holds that the ban imposed by the Government should have a reasonable basis and must have some relation to his suitability for employment or appointment to an office.
